{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Fred Stephen Roberts''' (born June 19, 1943)<ref name="cv">[http://dimacs.rutgers.edu/People/Staff/froberts/FredCV12-23-09.pdf Curriculum vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200110215600/http://archive.dimacs.rutgers.edu/People/Staff/froberts/FredCV12-23-09.pdf |date=2020-01-10 }} from Roberts' web site, retrieved 2010-02-16.</ref> is an American [[mathematician]], a professor of mathematics at [[Rutgers University]], and a former director of [[DIMACS]].

==Biography==
Roberts did his undergraduate studies at [[Dartmouth College]],<ref name="cv"/> and received his Ph.D. from [[Stanford University]] in 1968; his [[doctoral advisor]] was [[Dana Scott]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Fred Stephen Roberts|5937}}.</ref> After holding positions at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[RAND]], and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], he joined the Rutgers faculty in 1972.<ref name="cv"/>

He has been vice president of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] twice, in 1984 and 1986, and has been director of DIMACS since 1996.<ref name="cv"/>

==Research==
Roberts' research concerns [[graph theory]] and [[combinatorics]], and their applications in modeling problems in the [[social science]]s and [[biology]].<ref name="cv"/> Among his contributions to pure mathematics, he is known for introducing the concept of [[boxicity]], the minimum dimension needed to represent a given [[undirected graph]] as an [[intersection graph]] of axis-parallel [[box (shape)|boxes]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Roberts | first = F. S.
 | contribution = On the boxicity and cubicity of a graph
 | title = Recent Progress in Combinatorics
 | editor-first = W. T. | editor-last = Tutte | editor-link = W. T. Tutte
 | publisher = Academic Press | isbn = 978-0-12-705150-5
 | year = 1969 | pages = 301–310}}.</ref>

==Books==
Roberts is the author or co-author of the following books:<ref>[http://dimacs.rutgers.edu/People/Staff/froberts/BooksAuthored.html Books authored by Fred S. Roberts], retrieved 2010-02-16.</ref>
*''Discrete Mathematical Models, with Applications to Social, Biological and Environmental Problems'', Prentice-Hall, 1976, {{ISBN|978-0-13-214171-0}}. Russian translation, Nauka, 1986.
*''Graph Theory and its Applications to the Problems of Society'', CBMS-NSF Regional Conference Series in Applied Mathematics 29, [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]], 1987, {{ISBN|978-0-89871-026-7}}.
*''Measurement Theory, with Applications to Decisionmaking, Utility, and the Social Sciences'', Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications 7, Addison-Wesley, 1979, {{ISBN|978-0-201-13506-0}}.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Fishburn, Peter C.|authorlink=Peter C. Fishburn|title=Review of ''Measurement theory: with applications to decisionmaking, utility, and the social sciences'' by Fred S. Roberts|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|year=1981|volume=4|issue=2|pages=233–235|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1981-04-02/S0273-0979-1981-14893-X/S0273-0979-1981-14893-X.pdf|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-1981-14893-x|doi-access=free}}</ref> Reprinted by Cambridge University Press, 2009.
*''Applied Combinatorics'', Prentice-Hall, 1984. 2nd edition (with B. Tesman), 2004, {{ISBN|978-0-13-079603-5}}. 3rd edition, Chapman & Hall, 2009. Chinese translation, Pearson Education Asia, 2005 and 2007.

He is also the editor of nearly 20 edited volumes.<ref>[http://dimacs.rutgers.edu/People/Staff/froberts/BooksEdited.html Books edited by Fred S. Roberts], retrieved 2010-02-16.</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Roberts received the [[ACM SIGACT]] Distinguished Service Prize in 1999. In 2001, he won the [[National Science Foundation]] Science and Technology Centers Pioneer Award for "pioneering the science and technology center concept".<ref>[http://dimacs.rutgers.edu/People/Staff/froberts/Award.html Fred Roberts receives NSF Science and Technology Centers Pioneer Award], retrieved 2010-02-16.</ref> In 2003, DIMACS held a Conference on Applications of Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science, in honor of Roberts' 60th birthday.<ref>[http://dimacs.rutgers.edu/Workshops/Applications/program.html Conference on Applications of Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science], retrieved 2010-02-16.</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-07-07.</ref>
